{{Quote|Chandrila is a jewel of the Core Worlds but has historically harbored factions of dissent and treason.|Colonel Maximilian Veers, ''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''|<ref name="Handbook" />}}
'''Chandrila''' was an [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] located in the [[Chandrila system/Legends|Chandrila system]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds']] [[Bormea sector/Legends|Bormea sector]]. The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] had two continents and two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]—[[Chandra/Legends|Chandra]] and [[Chandrakant/Legends|Chandrakant]]—and lay on the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]]. The world was relatively rural, though it had 1.2 billion [[Chandrilan/Legends|residents]] and was home to several [[City/Legends|cities]].

The planet was an early member of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and remained a member for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]], except during a brief conquest in the [[New Sith Wars]]. Chandrila hosted the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic's]] [[Third Mid Rim Army]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a conflict which saw a [[Damotite bioweapon|bioweapon]] attack on its [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Hanna City/Legends|Hanna City]].

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was [[Declaration of a New Order|formed]] from the Republic, Chandrila was absorbed into the new [[New Order/Legends|regime]]. A series of Imperial-appointed [[Governor/Legends|governors]] were placed in charge of the planet; nonetheless, the democratic [[Chandrilan House]]—a council composed of the governors of each of the planet's cities—was not dissolved, and opposition to the Empire remained strong among the democratically inclined populace. Two Chandrilan [[Senator/Legends|Senators]]—first [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and then [[Canna Omonda]]—were harsh critics of the Empire. The first was forced to resign from the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], while Omonda, [[Gender/Legends|her]] replacement, was eventually [[Death/Legends|executed]]. Harsh agricultural tariffs were placed on Chandrilan products, and the planet was [[Blockade on Chandrila|blockaded]]. However, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], of which [[Chandrilan resistance]] fighters were a [[Corellian Treaty|founding]] member, sent [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] to break the blockade.

Later in the war, when the conflict had turned in the Rebellion's favor, [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] sent another force to [[Blockade of Chandrila|blockade]] Chandrila, which he hoped to use as a bargaining chip. The plan ultimately failed, and Chandrila became a part of the newly [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|formed]] [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. It remained a part of the Republic through the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] and was able to avoid invasion.

==Description==
===Geography and astrogeography===
{{Quote|Only after I was living in the forest on Pzob I realized how much I loved it, how much I'd missed the woods and the trees of Chandrila.|Triv Pothman reminiscing about Chandrila|<ref name="Children">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>}}
Located in the [[Chandrila system/Legends|Chandrila system]], a part of the [[Ringali Shell]] portion of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds']] [[Bormea sector/Legends|Bormea sector]], Chandrila was a [[Temperature/Legends|temperate]] terrestrial [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]]—a planet focused on farming—<ref name="Strongholds" /> with a [[Atmosphere/Legends#Type I atmospheres|breathable atmosphere]].<ref name="CatCW" /> The remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was one of the most sparsely populated in the Core<ref name="FF7">{{FactFile|7|PLA 1-6|Planets of the Core Worlds}}</ref> and was covered in plains, [[Forest/Legends|forests]], hills, [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]],<ref name="Strongholds" /> and gentle seas.<ref name="CatCW" /> Chandrila was kept far more pristine than many other Core Worlds,<ref name="Strongholds" /> and its beauty was regularly compared to that of the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="TEGtPaM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> Industry was only allowed in [[Emita/Legends|Emita]], one of the planet's largest [[City/Legends|cities]], though it was subject to strict environmental regulations.<ref name="Strongholds" />

[[File:Crystalcanyon.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The canyons on Chandrila in 14 ABY]]
Chandrila had a diameter of 13,500 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] and was orbited by two [[Moon/Legends|moons]], [[Chandra/Legends|Chandra]] and [[Chandrakant/Legends|Chandrakant]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> The planet itself orbited a [[Chandrila (star)|star]] of the same name<ref name="CatCW" /> and was located on the [[Bormea/Darpa Corridor]] section of the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]], eleven hours [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] by [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] from [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], eighteen hours from [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], ninety-two hours from [[Ralltiir/Legends|Ralltiir]], thirty-four hours from [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]], and sixty-one hours from [[Rhinnal/Legends|Rhinnal]].<ref name="Far Orbit" /> Using a military-grade Class One hyperdrive, travel times to nearby planets were shortened: two hours to [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], one hour to Corulag, five hours to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], three hours to Esseles, two hours to Rhinnal, and four hours to Ralltiir.<ref name="Fact File Map">''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File Collector's Guide & Galaxy Chart]]''</ref> Chandrila's location on the Perlemian put it on the border between the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] portion of the Core Worlds and the [[Arrowhead]], which constituted [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] region of the Core.<ref name="TEA" /> A day on Chandrila lasted twenty standard hours, while a year was 368 [[Standard day/Legends|standard days]] in length.<ref name="Strongholds" /> The strength of the planet's [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] was standard.<ref name="CatCW" />

The lush planet had two main continents—[[Ananta]] and an [[Chandrila's eastern continent|eastern continent]]<ref name="Strongholds" />—which were covered with [[Grass/Legends|grassy]], rolling plains. An idyllic world, Chandrila remained temperate year-round, with gentle winters and warm summers. Dry seasons were interspersed with mild drizzles, leading to a lack of drought, and even the winds were mild. [[Chandrilan/Legends|Chandrilans]] lived in harmony with nature, educated from birth in proper maintenance of a balanced ecosystem. Furry [[Squall (species)|squalls]] could be found wandering within cities, protected by law from harm. The planet's residents maintained game preserves where the forest's birds, such as [[blackback]]s, were hunted for sport.<ref name="CatCW" /> Chandrila's carefully managed hunting grounds were among the only such facilities in the Core.<ref name="Far Orbit" />

Sights on the planet included the attractive [[Gladean State Parks]], a [[Hanna Wild Game Reserve|wild game reserve]] near [[Hanna City/Legends|Hanna]], [[Brionelle Memorial Military Academy]], and a [[dacha]] owned by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] founder [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] on the shores of [[Lake Sah'ot]]. Just offshore of Hanna lay a spectacular [[Coral/Legends|coral]] reef.<ref name="CatCW" />

===Flora and fauna===
[[File:SquallSWG2.png|thumb|right|200px|A Chandrilan squall]]
Chandrila's native fauna were extremely important to the Chandrilan populace, and it was not uncommon to see wild creatures—especially the squall and [[fecklen]]—roaming wherever they wished. Other Chandrilan creatures included the blackback—a [[Bird/Legends|bird]] of prey—and the [[cairnmog]], a horned [[Lizard/Legends|lizard]]. Despite their overall protectiveness of the environment, Chandrilans hunted both cairnmogs and blackbacks (though doing so required an expensive permit) and [[Fishing/Legends|fished]] the planet's seas. The [[Equine/Legends|equinoid]] [[ghorla]] was ridden by Chandrilans and used to hunt the blackback.<ref name="Strongholds" /> One Chandrilan [[Big game hunter/Legends|hunter]] was [[Kylo Batta]], who settled on the planet and started a family with his [[Kaori Batta's mother|wife]] and son, [[Kaori Batta|Kaori]].<ref name="Wretched Hives">''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]''</ref> An [[Unidentified avian|avian]] creature with quicksilver wings also dwelled on the planet.<ref name="NJORebirth" />

Although much of Chandrila was covered by farmland, native plants could still be found on the planet. These included the [[Tintolive tree/Legends|tintolive]]<ref name="Strongholds" /> and [[sienta tree]]s, which made up part of the forest in the Hanna Wild Game Reserve.<ref name="CatCW" /> [[Balmgrass/Legends|Balmgrass]] and [[bristing]] lined the coast of the [[Silver Sea/Legends|Silver Sea]]. Chandrila was also home to a variety of [[Unidentified tree|tree]] with bark that was scored with [[Diamond/Legends|diamond]]-shaped patterns.<ref name="NJORebirth" />

==History==
===Early history===
{{Quote|But [Xendor] failed, and it was war—war on Chandrila and Brentaal, then Coruscant and Metellos.|Follower of Palawa Arden Lyn speaking in a debriefing to Imperial troops about the First Great Schism|<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Red-Reaper-Chandrila.png|thumb|left|300px|Chandrila during the Old Republic era]]
Chandrila was settled by [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]]—a [[Time/Legends|time]] that saw the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] first expansion in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]—and<ref name="Strongholds" /> in [[25,053 BBY]]<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' dates the founding of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to [[25,053 BBY]].</ref> became one of the [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founders]] that came together to form the Republic.<ref name="TEA" /> Eventually, Chandrila would claim that it was the first agriworld to join that body, although records were not reliable enough to confirm or deny that claim.<ref name="Strongholds" /> In [[24,500 BBY]], the [[First Great Schism]] began.<ref name="JedivsSith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> The Schism was a conflict between rival factions of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. During the struggle, a [[Battle of Chandrila (First Great Schism)|battle]] was fought on the planet,<ref name="TEGtW" /> although it was not a major battle.<ref name="Minor">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'' establishes that no major battles were fought on Chandrila for twenty-five [[Millennium/Legends|thousand]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after its [[Colonist/Legends|settlement]], meaning that the [[Battle of Chandrila (First Great Schism)|battle]], which is described as part of the First Great Schism by ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', must not have been a major battle.</ref>

At some point in the planet's history, a [[Chandrilan (language)/Legends|Chandrilan language]] was used on the planet. By the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], the [[Language/Legends|language]] was only used by academics, but its legacy lived on in the names of Chandrila's moons, Chandra and Chandrakant, which meant 'point' and 'counterpoint,' respectively.<ref name="Strongholds" />

===Age of the Sith===
{{Quote|The Library of Chandrila did uncover a Sith text, as they predicted. Our shadow agent on the scene disposed of the text. No one was harmed.|Haazen reporting to Krynda Draay on the text found in the Library of Chandrila|<ref name="KOTOR33">[[Knights of the Old Republic 33|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 33]]</ref>}}
Around [[4017 BBY]],<ref name="RaffaanDate">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' establishes that [[Keval Raffaan]] was seventeen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old four [[Millennium/Legends|thousand years]] before the events of {{Film|IV}}, which corresponds to approximately [[4017 BBY]] per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> future [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Keval Raffaan]] was born on Chandrila.<ref name="Kabus">{{WEGCite|story=Ruins of Kabus-Dabeh|book=Tales of the Jedi Companion}}</ref> 54 years later, in [[3963 BBY]], the [[Library of Chandrila]] discovered a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] document, which was quickly disposed of by an agent of former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Krynda Draay]] and [[Haazen]].<ref name="KOTOR33" /> Also in that year, the [[Moomo Brothers|brothers]] [[Del Moomo|Del]] and [[Dob Moomo]] were instructed by [[Jervo Thalien]] to find the [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvian]] [[Marn Hierogryph]] on the streets of Chandrila in order to participate in an operation on<ref name="KOTOR40">[[Knights of the Old Republic 40|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 40]]</ref> the Core World<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> of [[Taris/Legends|Taris]].<ref name="KOTOR40" /> Hierogryph came to the planet after he and his partner, [[Slyssk]], accidentally saved a [[Battalion/Legends|battalion]] of Republic soldiers during the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. He was commended by a group of [[Ministry of Defense]] officials there, who spun a false narrative about how "[[Benegryph Goodvalor]]" had saved the soldiers.<ref name="KOTOR47">[[Knights of the Old Republic 47|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 47]]</ref> During the Mandalorian Wars, Chandrila was represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by the [[Morvis (senator)|mother]] of [[Dallan Morvis]].<ref name="Web enhancement">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KOTORweben2|text=KOTOR Campaign Guide Web Enhancement 2: Captain Dallan Morvis}}</ref>

[[File:Markus_Thul.png|thumb|right|200px|Markus Thul settled on Chandrila.]]
In [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Thuldate">{{TOR_dates|1}} These events include the [[Desolator crisis]], during which [[Markus Andarius Thul|Markus Thul]] fled [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], so Thul left the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in 3643 BBY.</ref> the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Markus Andarius Thul|Markus Thul]] fled his homeworld with his [[Valyn Thul|wife]] and [[Altana Thul|daughter]], settling with his family in a [[Vine/Legends|vineyard]] on Chandrila.<ref name="Thul">{{TORcite|type=message|My Thanks|[[Markus Andarius Thul|Markus Thul]]}}</ref> Although for 25,000 years after its settlement, no major battles occurred on Chandrilan soil,<ref name="CatCW" /> around [[3642 BBY]]<ref name="TorDates">{{TOR dates|2}}</ref> a [[Battle of the Red Reaper|battle]] did occur on an [[Chandrila Orbital Station|station]] in Chandrilan [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] between the forces of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] and the Republic, which was aided by [[Chandrilan Security Force]] personnel. The battle ultimately resulted in the defeat of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Ikoral]].<ref name="Red Reaper">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|The Red Reaper}}</ref> [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Brionelle]] of the Security Force fought and died on the station, and a military academy on the surface was later named for her.<ref name="Strongholds" />

By the time the [[New Sith Wars]] broke out<ref name="CatCW" /> in [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the planet was able to import most of the industrial goods that it needed from other worlds while making use of [[agriforest]]s and automated [[agricombine]] [[Farm/Legends|farms]] to grow beans, [[Grain/Legends|grains]], and produce for export. The planet was also the location of a Jedi temple and the [[Burial/Legends|tomb]] of the third Jedi [[Barsen'thor]], a hero of the [[Great Galactic War]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> Although initially located in Republic space,<ref name="TEA" /> the world was [[Battle of Chandrila (New Sith Wars)|captured]] by the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] near the end of the New Sith Wars.<ref name="Path of Destruction" />

Chandrila's early settlers were particularly interested in preserving the planet's natural beauty and establishing a representative [[Democracy/Legends|democracy]]. They made sure to invest in education in the early era of Chandrilan settlement, which they felt was necessary to prevent anyone from infringing upon the people's power to self-govern.<ref name="Strongholds" /> At some point prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Chandrilans also established a colony world on [[G'rho]] in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], but it was only ever sparsely settled. One of its few residents was [[Dev Sibwarra]], who was born on Chandrila<ref name="TABSB" /> around [[11 BBY/Legends|11 BBY]]<ref name="SibwarraDate">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' establishes that [[Dev Sibwarra]] was fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old at the [[Time/Legends|time]] of his [[Death/Legends|death]]. Sibwarra's death occurred during the events of ''[[The Truce at Bakura]]'', which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. Therefore, he must have been [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] around [[11 BBY/Legends|11 BBY]].</ref> but moved to G'rho with his [[Ydra Kilwallen Sibwarra|mother]], hoping to avoid the Empire after the disappearance of another Force-user. Ydra Sibwarra, Dev's mother, had been working on a book that detailed the history of Chandrila's subversion at Imperial hands.<ref name="Sweets">{{WEGCite|story=Strangers with Sweets|book=The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook}}</ref>

===The Republic's Final Years===
====Palpatine====
{{Quote|My father arrived unexpectedly on Chandrila. He had me taken from the youth program vessel and brought to our ship. My mother and siblings were already aboard. After the launch I learned that I was being taken to Chommell Minor. Just as you warned. We fell into an argument…then, I'm not sure what happened—"<br />"Tell me what happened"<br />"I killed them. I killed them—even the guards.|Palpatine to Darth Plagueis, describing the murder of his father|<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Palpatineyouth.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The future Emperor Palpatine visited Chandrila.]]
As the [[Great Peace of the Republic|era of the Republic]] drew to a close, the [[Legislative Youth Program/Legends|Legislative Youth Program]], a mock senate for [[Youngling/Legends|children]], met on Chandrila to encourage [[Politics/Legends|political]] discourse among the young.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the future [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]],<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> participated in the program and had the opportunity to explore Chandrila's parks, wilderness, and farmland. In [[65 BBY/Legends|65 BBY]], Hego Damask, secretly the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], visited Palpatine in the [[Hanna Wild Game Reserve]], surprised to find that he [[Precognition/Legends|already knew]] that he was coming. Plagueis's [[Droid/Legends|droid]], [[11-4D/Legends|11-4D]], was also present for the meeting.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Plagueis realized that Palpatine was strong in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and encouraged [[Gender/Legends|him]] to seek freedom from his father, [[Cosinga Palpatine]]. Ultimately, Plagueis was able to get the younger Palpatine to admit his desire to rule over the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] and promised to help him. [[Standard week/Legends|Weeks]] later, as Palpatine prepared to leave the planet, he was surprised by the sudden arrival of his father, who took his son offworld using his own [[Starship/Legends|ship]]. Onboard the ship, Palpatine [[Death/Legends|killed]] his father, his [[Palpatine's first brother|two]] [[Palpatine's second brother|brothers]], and his [[Palpatine's first sister|two]] [[Palpatine's second sister|sisters]]. On Plagueis's advice, he then returned to Chandrila, the authorities of which questioned him. By that point in Chandrila's history, the planet's wealth was greater than that of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and comparable to that of the<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> Core World<ref name="TEA" /> of [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Years later, around [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]],<ref name="FarStarDarte">The ''[[FarStar]]'' was built around sixty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of ''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]'', which is set four years after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Nanda landed on one of the planet's continents and then walked to the childhood [[Mothma prairie estate|home]] of Rebel spy [[Kell Bircher]],<ref name="SW14" /> a member of the [[Chandrilan Special Forces]].<ref name="SW12">[[Star Wars (2013) 12|''Star Wars'' (2013) 12]]</ref> After reading several gravestones that lay next to the home, including those of [[Far Mothma|Far]], [[Finna Mothma|Finna]], and [[Artar Mothma]], Nanda realized that Bircher was part of the same [[Mothma family/Legends|family]] as Mon Mothma. Upon receiving this news, Vader flew the [[CR92a Assassin-class corvette]] [[Archer (Assassin-class)|''Archer'']] to the house and proceeded to fire upon it. Nanda, who was still nearby, received an enormous concussion and required medical care for three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] afterward.<ref name="SW14" />

Around the same time, the Alderaanian [[Noble/Legends|noble]] [[Cael Hanarist]] traveled to Chandrila in order to find and join the Rebellion, which he succeeded in.<ref name="AoRCR">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> At some point before the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]<ref name="TEGtW" /> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="TNEC" /> multiple Chandrilan families were assisted by Chandrilan authorities in faking their deaths in a [[Transport/Legends|transport]] crash. One of these families was the [[Farr family]]; two of its members, [[Samoc Farr/Legends|Samoc]] and [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn Farr]], immediately joined the Rebel Alliance as [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]].<ref name="TEGtW" /> Prior to the date 38:4:21 under the Great ReSynchronization, Chandrila was mentioned in the [[Smuggler's Handbook/Legends|''Smuggler's Handbook'']], a text published by [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] legend [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]].<ref name="PSG">''[[Platt's Smugglers Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:Alliance_of_free_planets.svg|thumb|right|300px|After the Battle of Endor, Chandrila became a part of the Alliance of Free Planets.]]
Around the time of the Battle of Endor in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Imperials deployed a massive invasion force that was ready to move on Chandrila, and had the Rebels not won the battle, the Chandrilans would have had only a few months before the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], another planet-killing Imperial battlestation, would arrive to destroy the entire planet alongside Mon Calamari.<ref name="TEGtW" /> After the Death Star's destruction and the Emperor's death, Mon Mothma signed the [[Declaration of the Alliance of Free Planets|declaration]] that created the [[Alliance of Free Planets]]—an interim government that would eventually [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|become]] the New Republic—on Chandrila's behalf.<ref name="TABSB" />

In the six months after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Empire withdrew all ground forces from Chandrila, cleared out and abandoned all of its facilities on the surface, and deployed seven Star Destroyers in picket formation around the planet. The Star Destroyers, along with support vessels, enforced a blockade, whereby all starship traffic to and from Chandrila's [[Spaceport/Legends|starports]] was forbidden. With the absence of Imperial ground forces, a provisional government allied with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] was formed, and though it was able to maintain order on the planet, it had little power against the blockade. As Chandrila held little strategic value, the reasons for the blockade were unclear to the New Republic.<ref name="R&R">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/sourcearchive/f20080213/index.html|text=Recon & Report}}</ref>

The ultimate reason for the blockade was that [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] hoped to use the planet as a bargaining chip against the New Republic's forces, though his plan failed after he was deposed by<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]]<ref name="TNEGtC" /> [[Ysanne Isard]].<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> New Republic officials had speculated as much, but they knew that their forces in the region were unable to match the Imperial Fleet and therefore let the Imperials be.<ref name="R&R" /> Because it was Mothma's homeworld, Chandrila was a target for the New Republic military.<ref name="RogueSquadron22" /> Shortly after the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|fall]] of Imperial-held Coruscant, Chandrila was liberated by the New Republic,<ref name="CatCW" /> and a proud Mon Mothma returned home.<ref name="TEGtPaM" />

==Inhabitants==
===Chandrilans===
====Personality and attitudes====
{{Quote|Chandrila has always encouraged and fostered free, responsible speech.|Governor Tanis Mothma during her response to a walkout at the Chandrilan Public Safety Commision|<ref name="HNN46" />}}
[[File:Squall_pack_SoR.png|thumb|left|250px|A Chandrilan with a group of squalls]]
Chandrila's inhabitants were known as Chandrilans and spoke primarily [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and [[High Galactic (language)|High Galactic]]. Chandrilans placed heavy emphasis on political education and encouraged political debates in the planet's public spaces. Chandrilans were known for their political candor and were often viewed by outsiders as being intelligent but unaccustomed to hard work<ref name="CatCW" /> and hypocritical for simultaneously condemning the industrialism on other worlds and relying on their purchases of Chandrilan crops.<ref name="Strongholds" />

Chandrilans tended to be quiet and contemplative in private situations while presenting strongly held opinions when in public. They made regular use of sarcasm during debates and arguments and, unlike some other Core residents, did not accept the precept that progress necessarily entailed separation from nature.<ref name="AJ7" /> Chandrilans generally enjoyed such hobbies as walking, debating, sailing, boating, yachting, and recreational fishing. Naval officers were particularly prone to boating and yachting. Most Chandrilan farmers owned [[Stun rifle/Legends|stun rifles]]. A source of pride for the whole planet, Chandrila's ranchers and farmers tended to be well-educated, politically active, and hard-working.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Chandrilans were also noted gardeners,<ref name="Far Orbit" /> and elaborate gardens were seen as a mark of high status.<ref name="AJ7" /> Those Chandrilans who had attended the Brionelle Academy were well-educated and often became pillars of their local communities.<ref name="Strongholds" />

During the Imperial Era, the planet's ties to the Rebel Alliance made it even easier for outsiders to criticize its populace. Though not all Chandrilans were Rebels, it was true that Alderaanians and Chandrilans made up a large percentage of Rebel Alliance personnel and that most Chandrilans at least disapproved of Imperial policy and sympathized with the Rebellion.<ref name="Strongholds" /> A few Chandrilans, however, argued vigorously in support of the body,<ref name="AoRCR" /> or even joined its [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]], as did Colonel [[Ardax]]<ref name="JAS">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> and Triv Pothman.<ref name="Children" /> Similarly, [[Dem Keval]] was appointed the Imperial governor of<ref name="Tasariq" /> the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]<ref name="EAOC" /> planet [[Tasariq]].<ref name="Tasariq" /> Two other Chandrilans, [[Kithriss]]<ref name="Queen">{{DoD|The Queen of Air and Darkness}}</ref> and [[darksider]] [[Savuud Thimram]], were close allies of Emperor Palpatine.<ref name="byss">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050414planet1|series=Byss and the Deep Core|text=Part 1: Byss}}</ref> Those Chandrilans who did join the Imperial ranks were often not able to advance very far due to their general lack of respect for authority.<ref name="Strongholds" />

Chandrilans who were members of the Rebellion ranged from its leader, Mon Mothma, to [[Jyn Freila]], a pilot,<ref name="Strongholds" /> to diplomat [[Thel Erelen]].<ref name="RebSource">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> The Chandrilan [[Engineer/Legends|Starship engineer]] [[Gen Tiraan]] was not a member of the Alliance but was a part of the [[X-wing development team|team]] that helped develop the Alliance's [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. Both Tiraan and Chandrila were mentioned in ''[[Wanted by Cracken]]'', a report published by New Republic general [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]].<ref name="Wanted">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']]</ref> Meanwhile, the [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] [[Edallia Monotheer]] and her husband worked to provide intelligence to anti-Imperial factions on Chandrila itself.<ref name="XWSC">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> [[Maarisa Zsinj]], mother of the Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]], was a Chandrila native and served in the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]]. After the Republic became the Empire, Maarisa scorned its corruption and became a pirate.<ref name="Despoilers1">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-1|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[File:MonMothma-RotJAVA.png|thumb|right|250px|Mon Mothma was the most well-known Chandrilan.]]

====Demography and education====
The 1.2 billion Chandrilans were overwhelmingly [[Human/Legends|Human]], with just 4% being members of other species. The planet's population changed little over time due to strict laws that were designed to help maintain the ecosystem. The laws were ratified by every city on the planet and prevented families from having more than one child unless they submitted special permits.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Even those families that had multiple children rarely had more than two.<ref name="AJ7" /> Nonetheless, the planet's citizenry swelled by thousands of individuals when Chandrila decided to accept numerous refugees from the Yuuzhan Vong War.<ref name="CatCW" /> Wealthy individuals regularly constructed retirement homes and holiday estates on the planet.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Both Mon Mothma and [[New Republic Intelligence/Legends|New Republic Intelligence Service]] operative [[Bhindi Drayson]] spoke with the same accent, which marked them as being from Chandrila.<ref name="RD">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines I: Rebel Dream]]''</ref> Some Chandrilan women, including Mothma, wore a piece of jewelry called a [[Hanna pendant/Legends|Hanna pendant]].<ref name="Pendant">{{CSWECite|II|14|Hanna Pendant}}</ref>

Because of Chandrilan settlers' early investments in education, by the Imperial Period education was widespread on the planet. And because Chandrilans' interest in education was deeply tied to politics—they believed that a well-educated population was harder for politicians or corporations to seize power from—political and legal knowledge were as common as knowledge of science and the arts. One major educational institution on Chandrila was the [[Chandrilan Academy of Sciences]]. Chandrilans of all social levels regularly debated one another in public spaces using advanced rhetorical techniques and commonly represented themselves in the planet's courts, which emphasized debate and negotiation.<ref name="Strongholds" />

===Culture===
[[File:ChandrilasRotunda.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Chandrila's Rotunda was a place of free speech and intelligent discourse.]]
The inhabitants of Chandrila tended to live in small scattered communities instead of large metropolises. Family homes regularly contained a flower garden, fishpond, or insect hive.<ref name="CatCW" /> Chandrila was regarded as a haven for art and culture among the Core Worlds planets.<ref name="FF7" /> Recreational fishing was popular on the planet, though it was tightly regulated by the government. In addition to fishing, Chandrila's government supported regattas and the [[Sun jammer racing|racing]] of vehicles called [[sun jammer]]s. One such race, held annually after the harvest, was known as the [[Chandrilan Cometary Games|cometary games]] and attracted racers from beyond Chandrila.<ref name="Strongholds" /> The [[Chandrila Equinoid Derby]] was another sporting event that shared its name with the planet.<ref name="Stay on Target">[[Stay on Target (sourcebook)|''Stay on Target'']]</ref> A slow and intimate dance from Chandrila had made its way off the planet<ref name="XIF">''[[X-Wing: Iron Fist]]''</ref> by [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]].<ref name="IFDate">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[X-Wing: Iron Fist]]'', which features a dance from Chandrila being performed offworld, to [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]].</ref>

Chandrilans acquired a reputation throughout the galaxy as arrogant and argumentative, due partly to their emphasis on political education and debate. Since Chandrila was a world with perfect climate and docile animal life, native Chandrilans were unfamiliar with the everyday struggles of life in less comfortable environments. Eager to share their paradisiacal way of life, they found resistance to their ideas baffling. Those who left their homeworld typically found employment as diplomats, negotiators, or artists,<ref name="CatCW" /> as did [[Opera/Legends|opera]] singer [[Amaro Fonteen]].<ref name="TEA" /> The right to protest on Chandrila was unparalleled, and Chandrilans took advantage of their right regularly. Political engagement and debate were similarly important in Chandrilan society; even the planet's moons were said to represent the value of debate and peaceful coexistence, as well as the importance of moving on when a debate was finished.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Chandrilan culture was considered contrary to the culture of the other Core Worlds.<ref name="AJ7" />

Chandrilan cuisine, which included the dish [[Chandrilan squall tendermeat]] with a fresh [[colla sauce]], was praised for its use of fresh, Chandrilan-sourced ingredients.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Two other items, [[Chandrilan herb tea]]<ref name="Galladinium" /> and [[Chandrilan hors d'oeuvres]], shared their name with the planet.<ref name="Skyewalkers">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]''</ref> The art of [[flat-sculp]], created by the [[Vaathkree (species)|Vathkree]] species, was popular on the planet, as were dance, spoken word poetry readings, live theater, and holovids. Museums, such as the Hanna Institute of Antiquities<ref name="Strongholds" /> and the [[Tagge Holographic Museum]] could be found on the planet.<ref name="Creatures">''[[Creatures of the Galaxy]]''</ref>

===Government===
All citizens had a direct voice in government and were known for vociferously arguing politics among each other. The planet was ruled by the democratic [[Chandrilan House]].<ref name="CatCW" /> The House was an assembly of the governors of Chandrila's cities, the most influential of whom was Jovive Centi. The House met in Hanna City, and although the body had floor debates, most legislative work occurred in private. Other governors during the Galactic Civil War included [[Millae]] of Nayli and [[Dehsea]] of Emita.<ref name="Strongholds" /> The Chandrilan House's sessions were rowdy and sarcastic, constrasting with the staid [[Rules of Debate|procedure]] in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. However, this apparent boorishness hid complex political maneuvering, especially by those members of the House who stayed quiet, for they often manipulated others from behind the scenes. Despite the Chandrilan House's legislative role, all Chandrilans were able to vote on major issues.<ref name="AJ7" />

So strong was the public's value of democracy that during Imperial rule, Governor Gerald Weizel chose not to disband the Chandrilan House. Although debates were largely civil, they sometimes became heated enough to lead to violence. Although Chandrila had little experience with open war, some natives were known to nurse grudges and even attempt assassinations, hence the development of personal weapons such as the datadagger. The Malkite Poisoners were an organization that carried out many assassinations on Chandrila.<ref name="CatCW" /> Despite the importance of democracy to the Chandrilan people, there was at least one noblewoman, [[Hella Cordoni]], who hailed from Chandrila.<ref name="Secrets">{{WizCite|story=Young love... such a pain!|book=Secrets of Naboo}}</ref> Another nobleman, Lord [[Haakon]], owned land on Chandrila but was forced to sell it by the [[Rebellion era]].<ref name="ND">{{WEGCite|story=Elusive (adventure)|book=No Disintegrations (West End Games)}}</ref>

[[File:Squall.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Chandrila's government earmarked funds annually to repair damage caused by squalls.]]
Each city was ruled by an elected official known as a governor. Over 1,000 governors held office at any one time, and the governors of many smaller communities represented their homes in the Chandrilan House. Individual cities had considerable freedom to create their own laws, and each one had a location in the city center—usually a rotunda, such as the [[Debate Rotunda]] in Hanna City—that was used for public debate. Chandrila had a [[Planetary Security Forces|planetary security force]], the Chandrilan Security Force, and a [[Navy/Legends|navy]], the Chandrila Defense Fleet.<ref name="Strongholds" /> The fleet made use of the Corellian corvette ''[[Stormstrike]]'', the crew of which included Chandrilan quartermaster [[Kylan DuPre]].<ref name="ThrawnTrilogySourcebook" />

Chandrila's government included customs officials who worked to prevent parasites and other invasive organisms from damaging the planet's ecosystem. The Galactic Empire also operated customs vessels in orbit until they were eventually driven off. The planetary government used its tax revenue to [[Gladean State Parks Fund|fund]] the Gladean State Park system and its [[Chandrilan Park Ranger Service|rangers]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> Every year, the government also earmarked funds for "[[squall maintenance]]," used to repair damage caused by the ubiquitous animals. The government also issued a [[Chandrilian positive ecology seal|seal]] of approval for squall farms on other planets.<ref name="Domesticated Squall" />

===Economy and infrastructure===
[[File:MujaFruit.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Muja fruit was one of several crops grown on Chandrila.]]
Chandrila was one of the few agriworlds in the Core and was one of the only ones that did not make use of [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]] factories.<ref name="Far Orbit" /> Chandrila specialized in crops that did not last long enough for long [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace travel]];<ref name="AJ7">{{JournalCite|7|Into the Core Worlds}}</ref> the planet's crops included grains, [[Muja fruit/Legends|muja fruit]], [[Jaquira fruit/Legends|jaquira fruit]], [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]], beans,<ref name="Strongholds" /> and [[Spice/Legends|spices]],<ref name="AJ6">{{JournalCite|6|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> all of which were widely exported, especially to other Core Worlds. Although historically Chandrilans grew their crops in fields, these crops came to be grown in orchards, vegetable farms, and vineyards, a change that was necessary to make in order to compete with other agriworlds, which were much less environmentally conscious than Chandrila. Chandrilan crops were often sold to fine [[Restaurant/Legends|restaurants]] in the Core Worlds prior to their harvest.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Squalls were sometimes smuggled off the planet for use as pets and meat on other worlds. Although this was technically illegal, the squall population was large enough that Chandrilan authorities rarely prosecuted the crime, though they sometimes issued small fines.<ref name="Domesticated Squall" /> Chandrila's major imports included high technology.<ref name="Far Orbit" />

Chandrila also grew the [[Chandrilan grappaberry]], which could be used to produce fine wines such as [[Chandrilan Blue '439]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> By the time of the Clone Wars, Chandrilan wines were found on worlds such as Coruscant<ref name="Jedi Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where the gangster [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] possessed fine Chandrilan wines.<ref name="Boba Fett: Hunted">''[[Boba Fett: Hunted]]''</ref> Chandrila also produced [[Chandrilan brandy/Legends|brandy]].<ref name="Strongholds" />

[[File:Cheyerooto.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Wookiee Cheyerooto worked on Chandrila as a bioengineer.]]
Chandrila's economy was dependent on the sales of its crops to other planets—especially to other Core Worlds—though it also did produce some manufactured goods of its own. Local economies across Chandrila were similary based off of ranchers and famers, who made up for their small families by hiring farmhands or buying droids.<ref name="Strongholds" /> By the Imperial Period, Chandrila was one of the largest [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] exporters in the Core and had practically cornered the Core's market on perishable luxury foods and spices.<ref name="AJ6" /> Although similar products could be sourced from the Mid Rim, Chandrila's were of higher quality.<ref name="AJ7" /> At least one [[Bioengineering/Legends|bio-engineer]], the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Cheyerooto]], gained renown while working on Chandrila.<ref name="Rage" /> Chandrila was also a tourist destination.<ref name="Strongholds" />

Because Chandrila's major settlements and farming communities were so spread out, a system of [[Hovertrain/Legends|hovertrains]] was built across the planet. These trains, which because of their [[repulsorfield generator post]]s could reach speeds of up to 200 [[Kilometer per hour/Legends|kilometers per hour]], were used to carry people and goods, especially to the planet's spaceports. Only three spaceports existed on Chandrila, though the largest, the [[Hanna City Spaceport]], was capable of landing ships of up to 600 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length.<ref name="Strongholds" /> The travel agency [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] carried passengers from other planets to Hanna's spaceport.<ref name="Star Tours">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref> Roads on Chandrila were sparse, and both livestock and wild squalls were allowed to be on them, which sometimes caused traffic jams.<ref name="TEGtPaM" />

===Individual Chandrilans===
[[File:Sulijo_Warde_CotG_Tony_Foti.png|thumb|left|200px|Chandrilan Jedi Suljo Warde]]
Multiple Chandrilans, such as [[Suljo Warde]],<ref name="Chronicles">''[[Chronicles of the Gatekeeper]]''</ref> [[Avan Post]],<ref name="CSWEChandrila" /> Keval Raffaan,<ref name="Kabus" /> and Octa Ramis joined the ranks of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Fury" /> Many others, including Mon Mothma, Admiral Hiram Drayson,<ref name="ThrawnTrilogySourcebook" /> [[Slicer/Legends|slicer]] [[Gowan Ch'lessan]],<ref name="Do No Harm">{{JournalCite|10|Do No Harm}}</ref> and [[Corporal/Legends|Corporal]] [[Midge]], were members of the Alliance to Restore the Republic.<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Corporal Midge}}</ref> [[Aelon Reglis]] was a Chandrilan male who ultimately became a gambler and traveled in his starship, the [[Adventurer (Crescent-class)|''Adventurer'']], until he gifted it to his daughter, [[Lynx Reglis|Lynx]].<ref name="Stock">''[[Stock Ships]]''</ref> By [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]],<ref name="Passages Date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of {{JournalCite|7|Passages}} to [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]].</ref> Chandrilan [[Pira Bland]] had become a spice smuggler operating on Tatooine.<ref name="Passages">{{JournalCite|7|Passages}}</ref> The shipping magistrate [[Halbard]] was a Chandrilan.<ref name="AJ7" /> [[Birrge]] was a Chandrilan who worked as a sanitation worker on Chandrila during the Imperial Period.<ref name="PSG" /> [[Zurel Hoban]], an Imperial pilot crewman, grew up on Chandrila and was the son of an aide to one of Chandrila's senators.<ref name="Murder">"[[Murder on the Executor|Murder on the ''Executor'']]"</ref>

Mon Mothma was born on Chandrila and raised in Hanna City, of which her mother was governor. Her [[Mon Mothma's father/Legends|father]] served the Republic as an [[Arbiter-general/Legends|arbiter-general]]. Mothma joined the Republic's Senate while still a teenager and, after the body was reformed as the Imperial Senate, became one of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine's harshest critics. Ultimately, she became a founding member of the Rebel Alliance and eventually its [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|leader]]. When the Alliance transitioned to the New Republic, Mothma kept a leadership role, becoming [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] of the new government. During that time, she reminisced fondly of her time on Chandrila. When she returned to her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], she was welcomed as a hero and bought a [[Mon Mothma's dacha|dacha]] near Lake Sah'ot.<ref name="TNEGtC" />

==Locations==
===Topographical features===
{{Quote|I learned to love the Silver Sea.|Mon Mothma|<ref name="TKT">''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Hanna_City_map.png|thumb|right|200px|The Silver Sea]]
[[Water/Legends|Water]] was a salient feature of Chandrila's landscape. The [[Emerald Ocean]] was one such body of water, located between the cities of Hanna and Emita. The Silver Sea was another large sea, this one located right next to Hanna. Lake Sah'ot was also near Hanna City and was connected to the Silver Sea by the [[Jhanjaari River]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> The Silver Sea contained multiple reefs that teemed with life, some of which were visited by Gavin Darklighter, whose [[Sera Faleur Darklighter|wife]] was Chandrilan.<ref name="Ruin">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin]]''</ref> The [[Shashwaat Mountains]] were a mountain range from which the Jhanjaari River issued.<ref name="Strongholds" />

Chandrila also had huge [[Crystal Canyons]], with bridges and gaps connecting them. The [[Chandrila Jedi tomb|tomb]]<ref name="JKA" /> of the [[The Barsen'thor|third Barsen'thor]] of the Jedi Order<ref name="Force and Destiny Rulebook">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> could be found there.<ref name="JKA" /> Tours of the canyons were offered by the company [[Chandrilan Adventure Travel]]. Blackback birds hunted in the area,<ref name="Strongholds" /> and Chandrilan rebel [[Zal Artha]] raced speeders through the canyons.<ref name="AoRCR" /> Scholar [[Hethan Romund]] mentioned the canyons to [[Monk/Legends|monk]] [[Dao Jodh]] when describing various locations around the galaxy to him.<ref name="Dao">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Beginner Game|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Beginner Game]] (Character Folio - [[Dao Jodh|Dao]])</ref>

===Cities===
[[File:Hanna_City.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Chandrila's capital, Hanna City]]
Chandrila's capital was Hanna City, located between the Silver Sea and Lake Sah'ot. The city was founded as a small fishing village,<ref name="Strongholds" /> but it evolved into a metropolitan area. It was home to Chandrila's largest spaceport, an Imperial garrison, a [[Hanna City Harbor|harbor]],<ref name="CatCW" /> the Brionelle Memorial Military Academy, the [[Alderaan Expatriate Club]], and the [[Chandrilan House (location)|Chandrilan House]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> The Brionelle Academy trained officers for Chandrila's home defense fleet.<ref name="CatCW" /> Hanna was separated from the nearby Hanna Wild Game Reserve by the Jhanjaari River, which ran along its southern edge from Lake Sah'ot to the Silver Sea. Chandrila's bureaucracy was focused in the city, which also served as an academic center.<ref name="Strongholds" />

[[File:Nayli.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Nayli]]
Located on Chandrila's Ananta continent, Emita was another of the three Chandrilan cities that contained a [[Emita Spaceport|spaceport]]. The city was the only area of Chandrila that was zoned for industrial manufacturing, although its factories were still heavily regulated and [[Chandrilan industrial tax|taxed]]. Emita was home to the [[ChandrilTech headquarters spire|headquarters]], [[ChandrilTech warehouse|warehouse]], and [[ChandrilTech main factory|primary factory]] of [[ChandrilTech]], a major technology firm led by [[Hella Thimram]] and founded by her [[Hella Thimram's grandfather|grandfather]]. Emita also contained most of the Gladean State Parks, a planet-wide system of parks that were named for a historical [[Gladean|governor]] and included the Crystal Canyons, the [[Gladean Arboretum]], and the [[Gladean Gardens Botanical Park of Chandrila]].<ref name="Strongholds" /> The parks were renowned across the galaxy.<ref name="Force and Destiny Rulebook" /> During the Imperial Period, Emita's governor was Dehsea.<ref name="Strongholds" />

Nayli was centered on its own [[Nayli Spaceport|spaceport]]. The city was surrounded by [[Color/Legends|green]] hills, was located in the center of Chandrila's equatorial belt, and produced a significant portion of its produce exports.<ref name="Strongholds" /> Salline was a port city that was temporarily taken over by the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="Handbook" /> Located somewhere on Chandrila was a procession route known as [[Grand Avenue]].<ref name="Goroth">''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Starwarssourcebook1st.jpg|thumb|right|200px|''The Star Wars Sourcebook'' contained the first mention of Chandrila.]]
Chandrila was first mentioned in the [[1987]] ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', which was published for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="SWSourcebook">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> It made its first appearance in<ref name="Star Wars Rebellion">[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]</ref> the [[February 28]], [[1998]]<ref name="VisualHistory">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]; the image used in the game to represent Chandrila was also used to depict other worlds, such as [[Uvena Prime/Legends|Uvena]] and [[Geedon V]].<ref name="Star Wars Rebellion" /> The [[August 8]], [[2009]]<ref name="Penguin">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/185066/the-essential-atlas-star-wars-by-daniel-wallace-and-jason-fry|text=The Essential Atlas: Star Wars}}</ref> reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Chandrila in grid square L-9.<ref name="TEA" />

Chandrila has been erroneously named in multiple sources. [[Star Wars Galaxies: Rage of the Wookiees|''Rage of the Wookiees'']], the [[2005]] expansion of the video game [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], misspells the planet's name as "Chandrillia,"<ref name="Rage" /> while the [[September 10]], 2009 [[StarWars.com]] article ''[[Death Troopers: Recovered Messages from Purge]]''—a tie-in to the novel ''[[Death Troopers]]'', spells it as "Chandrilla."<ref name="Purgedate" /> The [[December 3]], 1998<ref name="IGN Profile">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/games/star-wars-rogue-squadron|text=Star Wars: Rogue Squadron|archivedate=20210630175457}}</ref> video game [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] and its [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide|official guide]], released the same year, erroneously refer to the city of Nayli as Chandrila.<ref name="RogueSquadron" /><ref name="StarWars: Rogue Squadron" /> The [[1995]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' by [[Andy Mangels]] states that Mon Mothma's mother was the governor of all of Chandrila,<ref name="EGC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> while later sources such as [[Daniel Wallace]]'s [[2002]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' describe her mother as governor of only Hanna City.<ref name="TNEGtC" /> This article assumes that the latter is correct.

[[File:Chandrila.jpg|left|thumb|280px|The appearance of Chandrila in ''Coruscant and the Core Worlds'']]
Inconsistent astrographical information for Chandrila has also been given. The [[1990]] [[roleplaying game]] source article "[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," published in the [[Voyages SF 13|thirteenth issue]] of the ''[[Voyages SF]]'' magazine, incorrectly places Chandrila in the "Chandril system" of the [[Relgim sector/Legends|Relgim sector]]. Since that article was released outside of the [[Lucas Licensing]] process, its [[canon]]icity within the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity was never confirmed.<ref name="Twinkle">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref> Later, ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' erroneously placed Chandrila in the "Sesswenna" sector,<ref name="Star Wars Rebellion" /> a misspelling of the Outer Rim's [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]].<ref name="TEA" /> Later sources such as [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[2003]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebook ''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'' established that the planet was actually located in the Chandrila system and Bormea sector.<ref name="CatCW" />

Another inconsistency concerns Chandrila's [[Hydrosphere/Legends|hydrosphere]]. West End Games' 1998 ''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'' sourcebook ''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'' describes the planet as having a "dry" hydrosphere.<ref name="Far Orbit" /> However, multiple sources describe and depict Chandrila as being home to oceans and seas, contradicting the earlier sources.<ref name="CatCW" />

===Non-canon content===
At the time of Alderaan's destruction, Chandrila operated an [[Chandrilan Embassy/Legends|embassy]] on Coruscant, which employed fifty-eight workers. Senator Mon Mothma was the planet's [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]]. [[Irem Gehldon]] worked as the acting ambassador if Mothma was absent.<ref name="HS24">{{CasusBelliCite|HS24|Il faut sauver Miss Pickalho}}</ref>

[[Jax Keyn]] was a Chandrilan freighter pilot.<ref name="Spark">{{ShadisCite|18.5|The Spark Before the Flame}}</ref>
